current: \label{sec:calib} \label{sec:uq2d} \label{sec:ll5d} Each coverage test in this section asks whether a covariance, rebuilt at a held-out truth by the reported procedure, covers the errors of pseudo-experiments drawn about that truth.

The target is the nominal content of each interval: per cell, the fraction of errors $e_c$ with $|e_c|\leq\sigma_c$, which is \fvval{null-p0} for a Gaussian error, and jointly the fraction with $\chi^2$ below its null distribution's quantile at that content.

Because the drawn uncertainties are two-point or discrete, each test replaces the Gaussian content with one matched to its draws, and flags under-coverage when a count of the pseudo-experiments falls to a binomial threshold of that content; over-coverage is reported and is not a failure (\ssec{S9}{supp:tests}).

base: The test's false-flag rate under its null distribution is at most 0.0348 and 0.0363 per tune.

A descriptive decomposition, made after this result, shows where the $\chi^2$ sits.
Its mean splits into a part from the pseudo-experiments' mean error $\bar e$, $\bar e^{\top}C_T^{+}\bar e$, and a part from their spread $S$, $\mathrm{tr}(C_T^{+}S)$.

The mean-error part is \fvval{t2a-bias-share-ar23}\,\% and \fvval{t2a-bias-share-g18}\,\% of it at \fvval{f1-tune-ar23} and \fvval{f1-tune-g18}, \fvval{t2a-bias-ndf-ar23} and \fvval{t2a-bias-ndf-g18} per degree of freedom; the spread part is \fvval{t2a-spread-ndf-ar23} and \fvval{t2a-spread-ndf-g18} per degree of freedom, where 1 would mean that $C_T$ describes the spread.

In $C_T$'s eigenbasis, the \fvval{t2a-ntop} directions with the largest eigenvalues carry under \SI{1}{\percent} of the mean-error part, and the directions beyond the \fvval{t2a-r1} largest carry \fvval{t2a-beyond1-ar23}\,\% and \fvval{t2a-beyond1-g18}\,\%.
Truncated to its \fvval{t2a-r1} or \fvval{t2a-r2} largest-eigenvalue directions, the joint test still finds none of the \fvval{cov2d-ntoys} pseudo-experiments in its region at either tune.

The under-coverage is thus dominated by mean bias concentrated in the poorly determined directions of $C_T$, with the spread also exceeding $C_T$'s prediction, and truncation to the better-determined directions does not remove it; the decomposition does not establish the cause (\ssec{S9}{supp:tests}).

Truncated to the \fvval{t2a-r1} or \fvval{t2a-r2} largest directions, the joint test finds none of the pseudo-experiments in its region at either tune, against its truncated null's thresholds of \fvval{t2a-kj73-ar23} and \fvval{t2a-kj139-ar23} at \fvval{f1-tune-ar23} and \fvval{t2a-kj73-g18} and \fvval{t2a-kj139-g18} at \fvval{f1-tune-g18}.
Two eigensolvers agree on every component to at most $\fvval{t2a-dmax}$ relative, no rank is unresolved, and the truncated counts agree.
The decomposition locates the $\chi^2$; it does not establish why the test under-covers, changes no verdict, and says nothing about coverage at the data's point.
